mainTopic: Can an עובר acquire property? The מחלוקת of רב נחמן, רב הונא and רב ששת, רב ששת's proof from the ברייתא of the גר and its rejections, and a challenge from the משנה of a one-day-old heir.
overview: Before this section, רב נחמן challenged רב הונא from a משנה. The גמרא asks why רב הונא didn't answer that the משנה speaks of a gift set for 'when she gives birth' (לכשתלד). It answers that רב הונא holds even לכשתלד does not work. This leads to a three-way מחלוקת. רב נחמן says a direct gift to an עובר fails but לכשתלד works, רב הונא says both fail, and רב ששת says both work. רב ששת proves his view from a ברייתא about a dead גר's property, where a second taking was needed after the pregnant widow miscarried. אביי answers that ירושה comes by itself and is different from a gift. רבא answers that the first taking was too loose to count. The גמרא explains where those two answers differ. It then challenges רב ששת from a משנה that a one-day-old inherits. The answer is that this only concerns inheriting the mother's property to pass it to the father's sons. The גמרא then asks why an עובר does not inherit in that case, and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Why not answer that the case is 'when she gives birth'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests an easy answer to רב נחמן's challenge: רב הונא could say the משנה speaks of a gift that takes effect 'when she gives birth.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Let רב הונא answer רב נחמן that the משנה is talking about someone who said 'when she gives birth'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes a simple way for רב הונא to escape רב נחמן's challenge. It is setting up the next step, which will explain why רב הונא could not use this answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the giver said the gift takes effect only once the baby is born, the baby already exists when the gift kicks in. That could explain the משנה without contradicting רב הונא. The גמרא is asking why רב הונא didn't say this.

keyTerms.meaning: But let him say to him (why not answer this way?)
When she gives birth: the gift takes effect at the birth

phrases.english: But let him say to him
phrases.notes: 'Him' is רב הונא answering רב נחמן, who had challenged him from the משנה.

phrases.english: that the case is where he said, 'when she gives birth'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of רב נחמן's challenge to רב הונא by proposing another possible answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why didn't רב הונא answer that the משנה speaks of a gift given 'when she gives birth'?

steps.title: רב הונא holds that even 'when she gives birth' does not work
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא could not give that answer, because in his view even a gift set for 'when she gives birth' does not take effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא follows his own view, because רב הונא said: even if he said 'when she gives birth,' the baby does not acquire.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the suggested answer doesn't work for רב הונא. He holds that even the 'when she gives birth' wording fails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An answer only helps if the person giving it agrees with it. רב הונא holds that an עובר cannot acquire even with the לכשתלד wording, so that answer is not available to him.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning (consistent with his known view)

phrases.english: Rav Huna follows his own reasoning,
for Rav Huna said:
Even if he said 'when she gives birth,' it does not acquire.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 1 by showing that רב הונא rejects the proposed answer on principle.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב הונא holds that even with לכשתלד the עובר does not acquire, so he could not answer that way.

steps.title: Three opinions on giving a gift to an unborn baby
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא lays out the full מחלוקת. רב נחמן says a direct gift fails but לכשתלד works. רב הונא says both fail. רב ששת says both work.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: one who gives a gift to an עובר, it does not acquire. If he said 'when she gives birth,' it acquires. רב הונא said: even 'when she gives birth,' it does not acquire. רב ששת said: in both cases it acquires.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the full three-way מחלוקת about whether an עובר can receive a gift.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two cases: a direct gift to the עובר, and a gift set to take effect 'when she gives birth.' רב נחמן splits them. רב הונא rejects both. רב ששת accepts both.

keyTerms.meaning: One who transfers ownership (gives) to someone
Both this case and that case

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן: direct gift to עובר fails, לכשתלד works. רב הונא: both fail. רב ששת: both work.

phrases.english: For Rav Naḥman said:
phrases.notes: Here the word means 'as was said.' It opens the full מחלוקת, not a new point by רב נחמן alone.

phrases.english: One who transfers ownership to a fetus, it does not acquire.
If he said 'when she gives birth,' it acquires.
And Rav Huna said:
Even if he said 'when she gives birth,' it does not acquire.
And Rav Sheshet said:
In both this case and that case, it acquires.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן הַמְזַכֶּה לְעוּבָּר לֹא קָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the full background of the רב הונא view cited in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב נחמן: a direct gift to an עובר fails, but לכשתלד works. רב הונא: both fail. רב ששת: both work.

steps.title: רב ששת brings a ברייתא about a dead גר's property
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת cites a ברייתא. People took a dead גר's property, then heard he had a son or a pregnant wife, and had to return it. If they later heard the son died or the wife miscarried, only a new taking counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: How do I know this? From a ברייתא. A גר died and Jews plundered his property. Then they heard he had a son, or that his wife was pregnant, so they must return it. They returned everything. Later they heard the son died, or the wife miscarried. Whoever took it the second time acquires it. Whoever took it only the first time does not.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת begins proving his view by quoting a ברייתא. This step lays out the case, and the next step will draw the proof from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking the property only works when no heir exists. The ברייתא treats a pregnant wife just like an existing son: the property must go back. Only taking it again after the miscarriage counts.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say it? (introducing a proof)

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
From where do I say it?
As it is taught in a baraita:
A convert who died,
and Jews plundered his property,
and they heard that he has a son
or that his wife was pregnant,
they are obligated to return it.
They returned everything,
and afterward they heard
that his son died
or that his wife miscarried,
one who took possession the second time acquires;
but one who took possession only the first time does not acquire.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב ששת begins supporting his view from step 3 that an עובר acquires.
steps.raayaObject: רב ששת's view that an עובר can acquire.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a גר's plundered property and a pregnant widow who later miscarried.

steps.title: Why a second taking proves the unborn baby owned the property
steps.stepSummary: If an עובר could not acquire, the first taking would have been fine and no second taking would be needed. So the עובר must have owned the property in between.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think an עובר does not acquire, why do they need to take possession a second time? They already took possession once!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת draws his proof from the ברייתא. The need for a second taking shows the עובר really owned the property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the עובר owned nothing, the property stayed ownerless the whole time, and the first taking should have counted. The ברייתא says the first taking doesn't count. So the עובר became the owner, and only when it was miscarried did the property become ownerless again.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it enters your mind (if you were to think)

steps.whatToRemember: רב ששת's proof: the ברייתא requires a new taking after the miscarriage, so the עובר must have owned the property in between.
steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is about inheriting, not about receiving a gift. רב ששת uses it to show that an עובר can own property at all.

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
that a fetus does not acquire,
why do they need to take possession the second time?
They already took possession one time!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ עוּבָּר לָא קָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the actual inference from the ברייתא quoted in step 4.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's rule that the first taking doesn't count and a second taking is needed after the miscarriage.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the core proof for רב ששת's view. The rest of the סוגיא will test whether the ברייתא really proves it.

steps.title: אביי: Inheritance comes by itself
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects רב ששת's proof. An עובר can inherit because inheritance passes on automatically, but that does not show it can receive a gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Inheritance, which comes on its own, is different.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רב ששת's proof from the ברייתא of the גר. He says that case was about ירושה, and ירושה is a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא the עובר owned the property through ירושה, which passes to the heir automatically with no act of acquiring. A gift needs the receiver to actually acquire it. So the ברייתא proves nothing about whether an עובר can acquire a מתנה, which is our question.

keyTerms.meaning: Comes on its own, with no act of acquiring

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying an עובר cannot inherit. He agrees it inherits. He only says this does not prove it can receive a gift.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Inheritance, which comes by itself, is different.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר אביי ירושה הבאה מאיליה שאני
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof רב ששת drew from the ברייתא in steps 4-5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof only, not רב ששת's ruling itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא is about ירושה, which needs no act of acquiring, so it cannot teach about a מתנה.

steps.title: רבא: Their first grab was loose
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different rejection. The second taking was needed because the first taking was weak and hesitant, not because the עובר owned the property.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It is different there, because from the start the property was only loosely held in their hands.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second, separate way to push back on רב ששת's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא explains the ברייתא another way. The people who took the property knew there might be a son or a pregnant wife, so their grip on it was weak and unsure from the start. That weak first taking did not count. This is why they needed a new taking, and it has nothing to do with the עובר owning the property.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that a קנין needs a firm, confident taking. A hesitant grab may not count.

phrases.english: Rava said:
It is different there,
phrases.notes: "There" means the ברייתא of the dead גר's property from step 4.

phrases.english: since from the start it was only loosely held in their hands.

steps.triggerLanguage: רבא אמר שאני התם דרפויי מרפיאן בידייהו מעיקרא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second rejection of רב ששת's proof, different from אביי's.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The second taking was needed because the first was weak, not because the עובר owned the property.

steps.title: What is the difference between them?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the answers of אביי and רבא would lead to different results.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a case where אביי's answer and רבא's answer would give different results. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both answers knock down רב ששת's proof. The גמרא wants a practical case where the two reasons would actually lead to different rulings.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two rejections just given.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where אביי and רבא would rule differently.

steps.title: They heard he died, but he had not yet died
steps.stepSummary: The difference: they heard the עובר had died and took the property, but it was not true. Only afterward did he really die.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them where they heard that he had died, and he had not died, and afterward he died.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the case where אביי and רבא would rule differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people took the property after hearing the עובר had died, but he was really still alive and died later. For אביי, the עובר inherits, so the property was not ownerless at the time and the first taking fails. For רבא, they believed he was dead, so they grabbed it firmly, and the first taking works.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them
That they heard he had died

steps.whatToRemember: אביי: ירושה comes by itself, so an עובר inherits. רבא: the first taking was too weak. Their answers differ when the takers wrongly believed the עובר was already dead.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them
where they heard about him that he had died,
phrases.notes: "Him" is the עובר, and "they" are the people taking the גר's property.

phrases.english: but he had not died, and afterward he died.

steps.triggerLanguage: איכא בינייהו ששמעו בו שמת ולא מת ואחר כך מת
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case where they heard the עובר died, took the property, and he only died later. For אביי the first taking fails. For רבא it works.

steps.title: A one-day-old inherits, so not an עובר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב ששת from a משנה that says a one-day-old baby inherits. That suggests an עובר does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: A one-day-old baby inherits and passes on an inheritance. A one-day-old, yes; an עובר, no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new challenge against רב ששת, who holds that an עובר can own property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה picks a baby one day old as the youngest one who inherits. That suggests that before birth, an עובר does not inherit. If an עובר cannot even inherit, how can רב ששת say it can acquire?

keyTerms.meaning: Inherits and passes on an inheritance

phrases.english: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: תִּינוֹק בֶּן יוֹם אֶחָד – נוֹחֵל וּמַנְחִיל.
phrases.english: A one-day-old baby inherits and passes on an inheritance.

phrases.aramaic: בֶּן יוֹם אֶחָד אִין, עוּבָּר לָא!
phrases.english: A one-day-old, yes; a fetus, no!

steps.triggerLanguage: תא שמע תינוק בן יום אחד נוחל ומנחיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new attack on רב ששת's view, after the proof for it was rejected.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's view that an עובר can own property
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה gives a one-day-old as the youngest heir, which suggests an עובר does not inherit.

steps.title: The משנה is about inheriting from the mother
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת himself explained that the משנה is about a special case: a baby inheriting his mother's property so it can pass to his brothers from his father. Only in that case does an עובר not inherit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Didn't רב ששת say: The baby inherits his mother's property in order to pass it on to his brothers from his father. And only a one-day-old does this, but an עובר does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The משנה is speaking about one special case, not about inheritance in general.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's point is that a newborn inherits from his mother, so if he dies, her property passes to his father's sons rather than to her own family. Only for this special case does an עובר not count. This does not show that an עובר never inherits.
steps.confusionAlert: "An עובר does not" here applies only to inheriting from the mother. It is not a general rule that an עובר never inherits.

phrases.english: But didn't Rav Sheshet say:
He inherits his mother's property,
to pass it on to the brothers from the father.
phrases.notes: These brothers share the father but have a different mother. They aren't her heirs, so they could only get her property through the baby.

phrases.english: And specifically a one-day-old,
but a fetus, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: הא אמר רב ששת נוחל בנכסי האם להנחיל לאחין מן האב
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the משנה to a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה teaches that an עובר never inherits.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה only teaches that an עובר does not inherit from his mother to pass it to his father's sons.

steps.title: Why doesn't an עובר inherit from the mother?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why an עובר is left out of inheriting from his mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why an עובר is left out of this special rule. The answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If an עובר can generally own property, as רב ששת holds, it seems odd that it cannot inherit from its mother. The גמרא wants the reason for this exception.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the limit stated in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why an עובר does not inherit his mother's property to pass it to his father's sons.
